title: 170+ versions later, I was able to create a cool RPG inspired by Aztec mythology, playable now!
author: Reckonerxy
selftext:
Hi [r/aigamedevI](/r/ClaudeAI/)! After a failed vibe-coding attempt on ChatGPT, I was finally able to build a playable game using Claude as a coding partner. After many rounds of iterative playtesting and debugging, I'm ready to start showing the game to the world!

Claude link: [https://claude.ai/public/artifacts/f5b6522a-7c74-4658-9006-991afbdf9c6b](https://claude.ai/public/artifacts/f5b6522a-7c74-4658-9006-991afbdf9c6b)

What is it: Teotlan: Land of Gods is a turn-based RPG with roguelite elements, featuring gods from Mesoamerican mythology. You pick a Patron God (you start with 4 options and unlock more as you progress), then build a team to explore and complete 9 layers of Mictlan (the Aztec Underworld).

Core Features:

* Turn-Based Combat: Both the player and enemies take turns acting, with a focus on unit abilities and positioning.
* Capture or Kill: Defeated units always give you a choice: capture them to add to your team, or slay them for bonus resources.
* Sacrifice for Power: Captured units can be sacrificed to summon powerful ally gods. Build the ultimate divine team to conquer Mictlan.
* Prestige: As a deity, death is not the end. Collect Teotl to unlock powerful upgrades and make each run through Mictlan a little easier.
* 12 Playable Gods: Each god has a unique patron ability and special move. Can you collect them all?

About my dev process: I always start by writing a design doc and locking down the game logic before any code gets written: this gives Claude a solid foundation to build from and makes it much easier to catch hallucinations or inconsistencies. Once Claude produces a build, I play through the entire thing to catch bugs, note improvements, and prepare feedback for the next version.

If the game catches your interest, I'd love to hear your feedback: especially how easy the mechanics are to understand, whether the difficulty feels right, and how intuitive the menu navigation is.

comments.author: DrinkCubaLibre
comments.body:
Congrats on going through enough rounds to get it working.  
Are you able to put this on a browser or something, host it on github?

Two seconds of play tells me one thing: too much UI.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: Gamedev pro tip: start cutting. I know it sounds strange. But start cutting. On this screen alone I see way too much text, including flavor text and the word "Tecpatl" twelve times. Cut until you only have the essentials. They teach you this in gamedev school but not while playing with AI.

replies.author: Reckonerxy
replies.body: Actually this is from a completed game with all gods and features unlocked. When you start the game, information is on a much smaller scope, and you unlock more things as you progress. I do agree with you that I still need to streamline the UI and game text on the next pass.

replies.author: teamharder
replies.body: I'm with the dude on this one. Cut all non-essential text.

replies.author: Reckonerxy
replies.body: working on that, It seems that UI still needs tweaking. Thank you for the feedback.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
that's crazy. were you able to get players to test those iterations? do you have an idea of the player count?

Aztec mythology does feel like an untapped territory so good luck

replies.author: Reckonerxy
replies.body: I have been testing the game myself so far. Got a couple of people playing on earlier builds, but mostly I have working on my own. Showing the game to reddit helps me giving some fresh eyes to the project and continue polish on things I overlooked.

comments.author: Busy_Place6572
comments.body: Just played to the mini-boss. Good game mechanics. Pokémon but can sacrifice dupes for better units .. and when you lose, you can upgrade for a better run next round.  The game-feel is good.  It wasn't obvious how the unit elemental class affected the combat

replies.author: Reckonerxy
replies.body: Thank you!!! The elemental affinity is a feature you unlock later along the way, but I do agree it should be obvious from the start.

comments.author: fued
comments.body: that generic AI ui is going to kill the game

replies.author: Reckonerxy
replies.body: Game still in early WIP, so i mostly focused on testing the game mechanics, the ui is super basic and i do agree i need to improve too. Also that’s why i asked for feedback in an ai-dev sub :)

replies.author: fued
replies.body:
user experience is the first thing I would improve is what I meant.

If people are turned away before even hitting the battle part, you need to clean that up.

new users first minute on the application is everything, you want that first minute to be super exciting.

replies.author: Reckonerxy
replies.body: Yes i agree, FTUE is important and is something im currently working on to improve on my next pass. Currently i worked on the foundations and i think sharing my progress can help figure out what do next to make the game more welcoming to play :)

replies.author: fued
replies.body: yeah 100% focus on that flow, hard to even get proper playtesting feedback without it. Looks like you have a base to work off, now the other 95% of gamedev, polishing it up haha

comments.author: Useful_Use_6170
comments.body: cool, just the UI killing me lol to text based. have you tried cursor or codex?

replies.author: Reckonerxy
replies.body: Keep in mind that this is still an super early prototype and UI still pretty undercooked. Hopefully on the next version UI and FTUE feels more polished.

replies.author: Useful_Use_6170
replies.body: I really liked the capture / farm for resources honestly this polished might be a nice game Ngl. If your gonna go into assets try out Adobe firefly  I’ve had good luck with it making UI and assets.

replies.author: Reckonerxy
replies.body: Thank you for the feedback! For the prototype im planning to replace the emojis and some ui elements with pixel art of my own, i just want to make sure that the game play mechanics feel fun first and the ui is at least clear enough to go into deeper runs.

replies.author: Useful_Use_6170
replies.body: Yeah!  Core loop is good , player retention is good. 👍🏼 and even with minimal assets because assets are always added in the end once the important part is completed
